# CLI Lifecycle Checklist: Supervisor CLI (start, status, stop)

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review for operator CLI lifecycle, concurrent chromedp instances, registry sharing, metrics, and teardown.
**Created**: 2026-11-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are lifecycle requirements documented for all three operator commands (`start`, `status`, `stop`) with no undocumented v1 surface? [Completeness, Spec §Functional Requirements]
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements for the background instance owner (detached helper holding the browser session) defined in enough detail for acceptance without reading the plan alone? [Completeness, Spec §Clarifications, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK003 Are concurrent multi-instance requirements explicitly included (not only sequential starts)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001c, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK004 Are cross-terminal registry visibility requirements stated so `start` in one session and `status`/`stop` in another are in scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK005 Are operator messaging requirements enumerated for success, empty, not-found, and failure outcomes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK006 Are blank-page-only scope boundaries documented relative to future casino/game automation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Constitution §V]
- [x] CHK007 Do contracts or data-model artifacts define registry record fields needed to satisfy spec entities without contradicting the feature spec? [Completeness, Plan §contracts, Data-Model §Instance record]
- [x] CHK008 Are constitution delivery-workflow testing obligations reflected or traced in feature requirements (default tests vs external)? [Gap, Constitution §Delivery Workflow]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK009 Is "blank page" defined with an unambiguous navigable target (not merely "empty")? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK010 Is "real-time" / live `status` quantified with a refresh interval or measurable update rate? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK011 Is per-instance CPU and RAM scope defined precisely enough to exclude other instances' processes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004a, Spec §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK012 Are opaque instance ID format, uniqueness, and stability requirements specified for the full run lifetime? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK013 Is "promptly" / non-blocking `start` tied to measurable success criteria rather than intent-only language? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001a, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK014 Is interactive `stop` input behavior (empty input, cancel, invalid ID) specified with expected operator outcome? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 3]
- [x] CHK015 Is the term "instance owner" aligned between spec, data model, and plan without conflicting synonyms? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities, Data-Model §Runtime entities]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK016 Do concurrent-isolation requirements (separate Chrome + profile) remain consistent across user stories, FRs, and edge cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001c, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK017 Are no-capacity-limit requirements (FR-011) consistent with load-test success criteria (SC-002) without implying a product maximum? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK018 Do clarification answers match formal FR bullets (background exit, isolation, parallel start, metrics scope) without leftover contradictory text? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications vs §Functional Requirements]
- [x] CHK019 Does the plan's operator-facing CLI contract list only behaviors mandated or allowed by the spec for v1? [Consistency, Plan §contracts/cli.md, Spec §FR-001–FR-012]
- [ ] CHK020 Are success criteria and functional requirements aligned on concurrent start count and timing (SC-006, SC-007 vs FR-012)? [Consistency, Spec §Success Criteria]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK021 Can SC-001 through SC-007 each be validated objectively using documented scenarios without inventing thresholds? [Measurability, Spec §Measurable Outcomes]
- [x] CHK022 Is the 95% manual stop SLA (SC-003) bounded by defined preconditions (valid ID, healthy instance)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK023 Are empty-state acceptance requirements distinguishable from error states in success criteria? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, Spec §User Story 2]
- [x] CHK024 Does quickstart map validation scenarios to spec IDs so acceptance criteria remain traceable pre-implementation? [Traceability, Plan §quickstart.md]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK025 Are primary flows (start → status → stop) covered by independently testable user stories with Given/When/Then acceptance? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [x] CHK026 Are alternate flows documented (multiple instances, parallel starts, cross-terminal use)? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1–2, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK027 Are exception flows defined for failed browser launch without phantom registry IDs? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1 scenario 3, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK028 Are recovery/reconciliation flows specified when processes die outside `stop`? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §User Story 2 scenario 3]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK029 Are split-brain edge cases addressed in requirements (owner crash vs Chrome survive, or the reverse)? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for metrics temporarily unavailable per instance? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK031 Is behavior specified when `stop` targets an already-terminated instance? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK032 Are overlapping `start`/`stop` during `status` consistency expectations documented beyond a single vague bullet? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK033 Is stopping one instance required not to terminate siblings under concurrent load? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK034 Are performance expectations for registry concurrency and status refresh documented at requirements level (not only in plan technical context)? [Gap, Plan §Technical Context vs Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK035 Are isolation/privacy requirements for concurrent profiles stated in operator terms sufficient for credential-bearing future automations? [Coverage, Constitution §III, Spec §FR-001c]
- [x] CHK036 Is platform scope (Linux/WSL vs other OS) explicitly bounded in requirements or assumptions to avoid silent ambiguity? [Gap, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK037 Are observability requirements for operators defined (what appears on `status`, placeholder semantics) without prescribing implementation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-008]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK038 Is the shared on-machine registry assumption documented with enough operator-visible behavior to validate FR-003? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK039 Are dependencies on external Chrome/chromedp availability stated as assumptions or failure requirements? [Dependency, Spec §User Story 1 scenario 3]
- [x] CHK040 Does data-model state machine (`starting`→`running`→teardown) align with spec timing for `status` visibility and "no phantom ID"? [Assumption, Data-Model §State transitions, Spec §FR-009]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK041 Is the `starting` intermediate state and any timeout-to-failure policy specified at feature-requirement level or only in design docs? [Ambiguity, Data-Model §Reconciliation rules, Gap in Spec]
- [x] CHK042 Does hiding the worker subcommand from operators conflict with Constitution "CLI as operator interface" for any mandated operator action? [Conflict, Plan §contracts/cli.md, Constitution §II]
- [x] CHK043 Are orphan browser / orphan registry requirements mutually consistent (FR-009 vs external kill edge cases)? [Conflict, Spec §FR-009, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
